assumptions: Needleman-Wunsch with free end gaps and the IUPAC substitution matrix is the right model for a read against its reference.
limits: One read at a time; a read from elsewhere in the genome still aligns somewhere.
bio.jane/contract.noReading: An intermediate step: two gapped rows handed to verify_read, which grades them and carries the Verify panel's reading. The panel never shows an alignment ungraded.
bio.jane/contract.question: How does one sequencing read align to the reference, as two gapped rows?

description: Pairwise-align ONE sequencing read against a reference and hand on the two gapped rows, so the read can be graded. Needleman-Wunsch with free end gaps and the IUPAC substitution matrix — SeqTrace's aligner, the same call the trace editor makes, so a pipeline and the panel align a read identically. Leave `reference` unset to align against the record this step runs on.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

read.description: the read's bases — wire a trace reader's `sequence` output here, or paste them.

reference.description: what to align against. Unset, it is the record this step runs on (the open plasmid, or an upstream product wired into the subject).

name: align_read

alignedRead.description: the read with gaps inserted — wire into `verify_read.aligned_read`

alignedReference.description: the reference with gaps inserted — wire into `verify_read.aligned_ref`

identity.description: % identity over the columns where both rows have a base (gaps excluded)

mismatches.description: columns where the two rows carry different bases

referenceLength.description: the reference's ungapped length in bp — wire into `verify_read.target_len`
